content.title: About
content.content: The sausage biscuit sandwich with cheese is a quick, hearty snack consisting of a soft biscuit, a grilled sausage, and melted cheese. It is usually served hot, making the cheese gooey and the biscuit slightly crisp.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first versions appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as street food.
The sausage‑cheese combo is a classic in British “bacon butty” and American “hot dog with cheese”.
In some regions the biscuit is replaced by a croissant, creating a “sausage croissant”.
Vegetarian versions use soy sausages and vegan cheese.
The sandwich is often topped with mustard, ketchup, or barbecue sauce.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Both the sausage and cheese provide high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Meat products are rich in heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese supplies calcium that supports bone and dental health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates (biscuit) and fats (cheese, sausage) quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and dairy contain B1, B2, B6, and B12 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and processed meats are high in saturated fats, which in excess may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Milk allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with dairy sensitivities should choose lactose‑free or plant‑based cheese alternatives.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some sausages contain nitrites and other additives that can be harmful in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the sandwich in an oven or on a grill until the biscuit is golden and the cheese melts. Serve with potato wedges, coleslaw, or fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Store sausage and cheese separately in their original packaging at 0‑4 °C.
